messages:
Liam (support): :rotating_light: Customer A reporting sudden spike of 5xx on hosted inference API, most errors are coming back from rate limiter path. They think it started ~08:12 UTC. sample req_ids: r-8a9f3, r-a12b4, r-c33d2. Support ticket #2456.
Devin (sre): Can you paste an example response body? 5xx from rate limiter sounds like a dependency timeout or an internal misroute.
Liam (support): Here is one from Customer A: ```{
  status: 500,
  error: "quota service error",
  code: "RQL-500",
  details: "upstream timeout after 10s"
}``` They say when they get this it surfaces across multiple endpoints (generate, embeddings).
Anika (eng-runtime): :eyes: Quick hypothesis: the quota service backend is timing out and the gateway is translating that to 500 instead of 429. We saw a config change on quota-proxy two nights ago (timeout lowered to 5s in canary). Could be backpressure -> 5xx.
Maya (oncall): Paging oncall now. @Devin can you check the rate-limiter pods and recent deploys?
Devin (sre): On it. Running: `kubectl -n prod get deploy quota-proxy -o yaml | yq '.spec.template.metadata.annotations'`
Deploy Bot: Deploy event: quota-proxy v2.14.0 rolled to canary at 2026-03-14T23:10:12Z by canary-controller.
Devin (sre): Logs: `kubectl -n prod logs deploy/quota-proxy --since=30m | grep -i timeout | tail -n 50` -> ```2026-03-15T08:11:05Z quota-proxy upstream request timed out to quota-orch/10.142.0.23:8080 after 5s
2026-03-15T08:11:05Z quota-proxy returning 500 to gateway request_id=r-8a9f3
2026-03-15T08:11:08Z quota-proxy upstream request timed out to quota-orch/10.142.0.25:8080 after 5s```
Liam (support): Customer A says their traffic is steady, but spike of error rate started ~08:10. They already disabled retries client-side to avoid extra load.
Anika (eng-runtime): That log shows quota-proxy had timeout set to 5s and returned 500. We should make the proxy map upstream timeouts to 429 for quota failures, or at least 503 for overload. Right now it's a 500 generic.
Maya (oncall): Immediate mitigation: roll back the canary timeout change to previous config (10s), and enable strict mapping so quota-timeout->429. Can we do a rollback?
Devin (sre): Opening rollback: `kubectl -n prod set image deploy/quota-proxy quota-proxy=redwood/quota-proxy:v2.13.7` and patch configmap: `kubectl -n prod patch configmap quota-proxy-config --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/timeout","value":"10000"}]'`
Deploy Bot: Rollback initiated by Devin at 2026-03-15T08:19:02Z. Canary drained.
Devin (sre): After rollback, I'm seeing fewer timeouts in logs. `kubectl -n prod logs deploy/quota-proxy --since=5m | grep -i timeout` -> no new matches.
Liam (support): Customer A reports errors dropped from ~18% to ~2% within 6m after rollback. :thumbsup:
Anika (eng-runtime): We need a permanent fix: 1) ensure quota service has circuit-breaker and increased capacity under burst; 2) map upstream timeout->429 or 503 depending on reason; 3) add e2e test that covers timeout-to-status mapping; 4) adjust autoscaler for quota-orch.
Maya (oncall): Agreed. Also we need a short-term customer-facing note from support. Liam can you send update and keep monitoring?
Liam (support): Yep. Sent Customer A: "We identified a recent canary change to the quota proxy that tightened upstream timeouts; we rolled back and errors dropped. We'll follow up with permanent fix and post-mortem"
Billing Bot: Alert: Customer A usage spike detected, billing telemetry unaffected but we should flag for review if errors recur.
Devin (sre): Follow-ups I will own: - validate autoscaler metrics (cpu/latency) for quota-orch - add tracing for forwarded requests to quota-backend - run soak test with 2x peak QPS
Anika (eng-runtime): I will own code changes: - change mapping in gateway: `if upstream == quota && err == timeout -> return 429 with reason: quota_timeout` - add test in integration suite.
Maya (oncall): Can we add a temporary circuit-breaker config to short-circuit requests to quota when it exceeds 95th percentile latency? That would allow us to return 429 early instead of waiting for 5s and returning 500.
Devin (sre): Yep. Will add `max_latency_threshold_ms: 3000` rule to proxy in next patch and push a canary. I'll run a small canary with 5% traffic first.
Liam (support): I'll collect customer logs / exact request ids for the PM. Please include them in postmortem.
Customer A (acct-team): Thanks for quick response — appreciate rollback and updates. We'll keep monitoring from our side and escalate if it reappears.
Anika (eng-runtime): Postmortem checklist: timeline, root cause (timeout override in canary), impact (failed requests %), fix (rollback + mapping + CB), tests, deploy plan. Assign owners and ETA.
Maya (oncall): Closing loop: incident severity P2, mitigated by rollback. I'll schedule a follow-up runbook update and postmortem in #postmortems once owners add details.
Liam (support): Marking support ticket #2456 as 'mitigated' and notifying account. Will add postmortem link when ready. :white_check_mark:
